examples.en: I peeled the apple thinly with a fruit knife.

examples.ko: 과일칼은 손잡이를 꼭 잡고 써야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hold the handle firmly when using a fruit knife.
Please take a fruit knife out of the drawer.
The fruit knife got dull, so I bought a new one.
It's dangerous for a child to use a fruit knife alone.
I packed a fruit knife too when going camping.

explain: 작고 날이 짧은 칼이고 '과도'라고도 많이 불러요. 사과나 배 껍질을 깎을 때 써요. '칼을 쓰다', '껍질을 깎다'와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small knife with a short blade, and it is also often called '과도'. You use it to peel apples or pears. It pairs with phrases like '칼을 쓰다' and '껍질을 깎다'.

examples.en: I put tofu and zucchini in the doenjang soup.
The doenjang soup my mother makes is the most delicious.
I add cabbage and boil doenjang soup.
I kept breakfast simple with doenjang soup.
Could you give me a little more doenjang soup?

examples.ko: 이 된장국은 너무 짜서 물을 더 부었어요.
examples.en: This doenjang soup was too salty, so I added more water.

explain: 된장찌개와 달리 보통 국물이 더 많고 맑게 먹는 국이에요. 된장찌개는 건더기가 많고 더 걸쭉하게 끓이는 경우가 많아요. 배추, 시금치, 두부 같은 재료를 넣어요.
explain_en: Compared with 된장찌개, it is usually a soup with more, lighter broth. 된장찌개 is often thicker and has more ingredients. Typical additions are cabbage, spinach and tofu.

examples.en: In a hurry, I put my wallet in my jeans' back pocket.
The phone in my back pocket got pressed against the chair.

examples.ko: 오래 입은 바지 뒷주머니의 단추가 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The button on the back pocket of my old pants came off.
When I went to do laundry, I found a receipt in the back pocket.
You have to be careful with a back pocket when you sit.
These jeans have big back pockets.

explain: 바지 뒤쪽에 달린 주머니예요. 앞쪽 주머니는 '앞주머니'라고 해요. 청바지 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the pocket on the back of trousers. The pocket on the front is '앞주머니'. It comes up often when talking about jeans.

examples.en: Someone is waiting outside the door.
It's cold, so I don't want to go outside.
The child ran out through the door.

examples.ko: 문밖의 소리가 시끄러워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The noise outside the door was loud, so I couldn't sleep.
Please leave the package outside the door.
It had snowed, so everything outside the door was white.

explain: 문 바로 바깥쪽을 말할 때 써요. 집 전체의 바깥은 '집 밖'이나 '바깥'이라고 해요. 보통 '문밖에', '문밖으로'처럼 조사를 붙여서 위치나 방향을 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the area right outside a door. For the outside of a whole house, people say '집 밖' or '바깥'. It usually takes particles, as in '문밖에' or '문밖으로', to show location or direction.

examples.en: Could you sign here?
I read the contract carefully before signing it.
The singer carefully signed every album for the fans.

examples.ko: 택배 기사님이 받는 사람 칸에 사인하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The delivery driver told me to sign in the recipient box.
I'll give it back after I sign the document.

examples.ko: 아직 사인하지 않아서 계약이 안 끝났어요.
examples.en: The contract is not done because I haven't signed yet.

explain: 서류와 계약서에는 공식적인 '서명하다'를 쓰고, 일상 대화나 유명인이 팬에게 해 주는 것에는 '사인하다'를 많이 써요. 표기는 '사인'이 맞고 '싸인'은 틀려요. '사인회'처럼 다른 말과 붙는 단어도 많아요.
explain_en: For documents and contracts the formal word is '서명하다', while '사인하다' is common in daily talk and for celebrities signing for fans. The correct spelling is '사인', not '싸인'. It also appears in words like '사인회' (a fan signing event).

p.n: 서명하다 is more formal, for documents.

examples.ko: 저는 숟갈로 국을 떠먹는 게 편해요.
examples.en: I find it easier to eat soup with a spoon.

examples.ko: 식당에서 숟갈 하나만 더 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the restaurant for just one more spoon.
I taught my child how to use a spoon.
I ate one more spoonful of rice.
I put the spoon and chopsticks on the table.
The spoon was too hot, so I put it down for a moment.

explain: '숟갈'은 '숟가락'을 줄인 말이에요. 말할 때는 '숟가락'이 더 자주 들리지만, '밥 한 숟갈'처럼 양을 말할 때는 '숟갈'도 잘 써요. 숟가락과 젓가락을 합쳐서 '수저'라고 하고, 식당에서는 '수저 주세요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 숟갈 is a shortened form of 숟가락. In speech 숟가락 is heard more often, but 숟갈 is common when talking about amounts, as in '밥 한 숟갈'. Spoon and chopsticks together are called 수저, and at a restaurant you say '수저 주세요'.

examples.en: The name is written on the front of the card.
The coin my friend tossed came up heads.
Please write your answers only on the front of the test paper.

examples.ko: 책 앞면에 예쁜 그림이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: A pretty picture is drawn on the front of the book.
Please write the address on the front of the envelope.

examples.ko: 옷 앞면에 작은 단추가 세 개 달려 있어요.
examples.en: The front of the shirt has three small buttons.

explain: 발음은 [암면]이에요. '앞'의 받침이 [ㅂ]으로 바뀌고 'ㅁ' 앞에서 다시 [ㅁ]이 돼요. 방향은 '앞쪽', 평평한 물건의 한 면은 '앞면'이라고 해요. '뒷면'과 짝으로 외우세요.
explain_en: It is pronounced [am-myeon]: the final 'ㅍ' of '앞' becomes [ㅂ], then turns into [ㅁ] before 'ㅁ'. Direction is '앞쪽' (front direction), while one side of a flat object is '앞면'. Learn it as a pair with '뒷면'.

dis.h: front side of a flat object

p.n: 앞 would mean 'in front of the card', so it is not a natural swap.

examples.en: Every night I hear music from the next room.

examples.ko: 제 친구가 기숙사에서 제 옆방에 살아요.
examples.en: My friend lives in the room next to mine in the dormitory.

examples.ko: 호텔 옆방에 저희 부모님이 묵고 계세요.
examples.en: My parents are staying in the room next to mine at the hotel.
I moved the luggage to the next room to clean.

examples.ko: 옆방에 사는 친구가 가끔 라면을 빌려 가요.
examples.en: The friend who lives next door sometimes borrows ramyeon from me.
The door to the next room was open, so I peeked in.

explain: 건물이 다르면 '옆집', 같은 건물 안의 방이면 '옆방'이라고 해요. 기숙사, 고시원, 호텔에서 소리 이야기를 할 때 특히 자주 써요. 발음은 [엽빵]이에요.
explain_en: A different building next door is '옆집', while a room in the same building is 'yeopbang'. It comes up a lot in talk about noise in dorms, small rented rooms and hotels. It is pronounced [yeop-ppang].

examples.ko: 장모님이 우리 집에 김치를 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother-in-law sent kimchi to our house.
My friend calls his mother-in-law every week.
I get along very well with my mother-in-law.
The whole family gathered for my mother-in-law's birthday.

examples.ko: 장모님은 사위가 오면 항상 고기를 구워 주세요.
examples.en: My mother-in-law always grills meat when her son-in-law comes.

examples.ko: 주말에는 장모님 댁에 가서 점심을 먹어요.
examples.en: On weekends we go to my mother-in-law's house and have lunch.

explain: 남편이 아내의 어머니를 부르는 말이고, 아내가 남편의 어머니를 부르는 말은 '시어머니'예요. 직접 부를 때도 '장모님'이라고 해요. 아내의 아버지는 '장인어른'이에요.
explain_en: It is what a husband calls his wife's mother; a wife calls her husband's mother 시어머니. You also say 장모님 when addressing her directly. A wife's father is 장인어른.

examples.ko: 설날에 온 가족이 모여 어른들께 절해요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day the whole family gathers and bows to the elders.
The child bowed politely to Grandfather.
I saw people bowing to the Buddha at the temple.
You bow first and then receive New Year's money.

examples.ko: 무릎을 꿇고 절할 때 손 모양을 잘 보세요.
examples.en: Watch the hand position when you kneel and bow.

examples.ko: 제사 때 어른들이 먼저 절해서 저도 따라 했어요.
examples.en: At the ancestral rite the elders bowed first, so I followed.

explain: 행동은 '절을 하다'라고도 하고 '절하다'라고도 해요. 설날에 어른께 하는 절은 '세배'라고 불러요. 같은 소리의 '절'은 불교 사원이라는 뜻도 있어서 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: The action can be said as '절을 하다' or '절하다'. The bow made to elders on New Year's Day is called 세배. The same sound 절 also means a Buddhist temple, so tell them apart from context.

en: gym clothes; workout clothes; gym suit

examples.ko: 내일 체육 시간이 있어서 체육복을 입고 가야 해요.
examples.en: We have PE tomorrow, so I have to wear my gym clothes.
Please write your name on your gym clothes.

examples.ko: 이 체육복은 작아져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: These gym clothes got too small, so I need to buy new ones.
My gym clothes got soaked with sweat, so I changed.
I put my gym clothes and sneakers in my bag.
The gym pants were too long, so I had them shortened.

explain: 학교에서 체육 시간에 입는 옷을 뜻할 때가 많아요. 일반적으로 운동할 때 입는 옷은 '운동복'이라고 해요. '체육복을 갈아입다', '체육복을 챙기다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It most often means the clothes worn in school PE class. Clothes for exercising in general are called '운동복'. Say '체육복을 갈아입다' (change into) or '체육복을 챙기다' (pack).

examples.ko: 미확인 메일이 쌓여서 편지함이 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: Unread emails piled up and the mailbox is full.

examples.ko: 편지함에 새 메일이 세 통 도착했어요.
examples.en: Three new emails arrived in the mailbox.
While cleaning up my mailbox, I found an old email.

examples.ko: 중요한 메일은 별도 편지함으로 옮겨 놓아요.
examples.en: I move important emails to a separate mailbox.
Spam emails were automatically deleted from the mailbox.
A notice popped up saying the mailbox is out of space.

explain: 이메일에서는 '받은편지함', '보낸편지함'처럼 쓰는 일이 많아요. 집 앞에 달린 우편물 상자는 보통 '우편함'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In email you often see it in '받은편지함' (inbox) and '보낸편지함' (sent mail). The box for physical mail at your home is usually called '우편함'.

en: to take heart; to cheer up

examples.ko: 조금만 더 힘내요, 거의 다 왔어요!
examples.en: Hang in there a little more, we're almost there!
A friend said 'Hang in there!' to me.
Let's keep it up and run all the way to the end.
I got my energy back after being cheered on.
The way you keep trying until the end is really cool.
I'll give it more effort in the next game.

explain: 응원할 때 가장 흔한 말이에요. 친구에게는 '힘내', 어른에게는 '힘내세요'라고 해요. '파이팅'과 함께 쓰는 경우가 많고, '힘을 내다'로 띄어 써도 같아요. 아주 슬픈 사람에게는 '힘내'라는 말이 부담이 될 수 있어서 '많이 힘들었죠' 같은 말을 먼저 하기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the most common way to cheer someone on. Use '힘내' with friends and '힘내세요' with elders. It often pairs with '파이팅', and '힘을 내다' written separately means the same. To someone who is very sad, '힘내' can feel like pressure, so Koreans sometimes start with something like 'That must have been hard.'
